gen-gf-sniglet-gf-noto-sans-old-south-ar: Distinctive from the first glance, Sniglet stops its terminals short of curling back, giving every word a level, unaccented beat. Noto Sans Old South Arabian follows gently.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-overpass: Sniglet's line is drawn with a single constant width, and its terminals stop short instead of curling back. Overpass keeps its strokes consistent inside every word, with e shapes that never clog.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-pt-sans: PT Sans reads open and friendly, its c forms sweeping as clear arcs. Sniglet is best at a commanding, one-stylus outline with stopped terminals, while PT Sans is best at carrying the actual text.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-quattrocento-sans: Modern and clean, Quattrocento Sans leaves a gap that keeps c from looking like o. And Sniglet, drawn like a plotter pen, gives it a bold single-weight headline to read beneath.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-rethink-sans: Round, blunt and friendly on top, Sniglet leaves its terminals short of curling while Rethink Sans stays generous below. Both keep one weight.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-roboto-flex: Roboto Flex opens its c with a wide slot. Sniglet does its best work as a commanding heading with wire-weight lines and stopped terminals, whereas Roboto Flex does its best work carrying everyday text in a plain sans.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-sarala: Sniglet leads with strokes that stop short of curling back in. Sarala follows in a plain sans with distinct gaps and neon-tube thickness, so a heading size well above the text looks natural.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-sn-pro: SN Pro keeps its aperture curves open through the whole alphabet. Sniglet is best at commanding, solder-smooth headings with stopped terminals, while SN Pro is best at modern, unfussy sans text underneath.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-suse-mono: Sniglet draws a rope-thin outline with no thick or thin parts, its terminals stopping short of curling back. SUSE Mono adds generous space around every letter.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-trispace: Trispace sets sparse, widely spaced letters whose curves open outward. Sniglet does its best work as a commanding bent-rod heading with stopped terminals, while Trispace does its best work quietly carrying text as a plain sans.
